name: lakatotree-judgement-receipt-engine
purpose: Own deterministic judgement, receipt, question-transition, and causal-outbox decisions for one LakatoTree aggregate while effect adapters retain explicit external capabilities.

fit_evidence: HTTP judgement and programme-cycle adapters already share stable verdict, receipt, replay, and temporal semantics.
One Neo4j aggregate head owns verdict state, receipt identity, question closure, causal outbox, and expected-head recovery.
The existing separate resource coordinator proves the command-to-decision pattern without becoming part of this state authority.
alternatives_considered: Rewrite every class as free functions
Create one engine per extracted planner

boundary.owns: Versioned verdict decisions, legal node and question transitions, receipt identities, replay-relevant facts, and causal effect requests for one LakatoTree aggregate.
boundary.mechanism: Transform one tree's immutable observed head and judgement command into a decision, transition, receipt plan, causal outbox, or typed rejection; commit facts before interpreting projections.
policy_outside: Deployment credentials, host selection, and retry timing
non_goals: Eliminating immutable dataclasses, Pydantic schemas, exceptions, or capability protocols
Calling clocks, filesystems, databases, subprocesses, or networks from pure planners
Changing durable wire identities during behavior-preserving extraction
boundary.state_authority: The writer-fenced Neo4j LakatosTree aggregate is the sole authority for verdict heads, receipts, question state, and causal outbox; PostgreSQL history is a repairable projection.

state_model: Versioned immutable command, observation, decision, transition, receipt-plan, and effect-request records; lifecycle FSMs remain the authority for legal node and question transitions.

protocol.versioning: Additive optional fields require presence-dispatched compatible readers; hash-domain, schema, event, or receipt changes require a new version and explicit migration while original bytes remain readable.

invariants: Equal immutable inputs and version identities produce equal pure decisions.
A pure planner imports neither lakatos.io nor server.
A successful public response is never exposed before the authoritative expected-head commit succeeds.
Receipt, event, hash-domain, and replay identities remain byte-stable during extraction.
Dry-run commands cannot reach live readiness, clock, mutation, or history capabilities.
OO remains only where it represents immutable data, schemas, errors, protocols, repositories, or effect adapters.

runtime.ordering: Commands are serialized by ledger scope or aggregate identity; existing database return order is preserved where observable.
runtime.concurrency: Independent aggregates may proceed concurrently while every mutation retains its expected-head or revision fence.
runtime.backpressure: Admission rejects or defers work at explicit queue, deadline, budget, and writer-readiness limits owned by the application shell.
runtime.cancellation: Judgement commands finish or fail within their writer-fenced transaction boundary; cancellation is honored before commit intent, never by exposing a partial verdict.
runtime.timeouts: External effects receive typed deadlines; pure decisions receive captured time only as immutable input.

durability.persistence: Append receipt-bound facts and outbox intent before exposing success; retain canonical bytes for replay.
durability.atomic_commit: Commit expected-head mutation, receipt, causal outbox, and relevant locks in one writer-fenced transaction whenever they form one invariant.
durability.recovery: Rebuild the aggregate from receipts, then reconcile pending outbox or projection records without minting duplicate verdict facts.
durability.effect_idempotency: Use existing content-addressed receipt, event, attempt, and effect identities; do not invent wall-clock-only deduplication.
durability.migration: Use compatibility facades and strangler slices; breaking durable changes require explicit versioned upcast or dual-read migration.

failure_model: Invalid commands and malformed durable snapshots fail without mutation.
Expected-head conflicts skip or reject exactly as the frozen public contract specifies.
Writer-fence loss and readiness failure remain typed external failures and are not converted to successful decisions.
A post-commit projection failure remains recoverable from the committed outbox rather than repeating the domain mutation.

traces: Command identity, observation hash, decision schema, receipt identity, commit result, and effect attempt share causation fields.
Compatibility facades expose the same public response while internal plan identities are available to tests and diagnostics.
metrics: Decision rejection and expected-head conflict counts
Outbox lag, recovery duration, projection retry, and effect failure counts
Per-slice OOPTDD mutation-kill and regression status
observability.redaction: Credentials and private payloads never enter plans, receipts, metric labels, or test fixtures; trace only bounded identities and hashes.

security: All ambient authority is isolated behind injected capabilities in the imperative shell.
Pure planners accept closed observations and cannot discover files, environment variables, credentials, or network state.
Mutation adapters retain authorization, writer fencing, containment, and fail-closed validation.
verification: Write RED-first guard_defect and guard_mechanism tests for every vertical slice.
Ship a hermetic OOPTDD receipt that drives real production code and a load-bearing negative oracle.
Run focused compatibility, full pytest, import-linter, compile, and Longinus binding gates.
Crash- and conflict-test commit/effect cut points before moving a durable boundary.
implementation_slices: Existing dual-resource decide/evolve kernel remains a separate engine and architectural precedent.
Stale-canonical immutable decision and receipt plan with the existing JudgementService CAS/history interpreter.
Submit-test-result receipt and causal-outbox plan while retaining its atomic Cypher interpreter.
Storage and production-readiness pure evaluators separated from live collectors.
Thin API, CLI, MCP, and composition adapters over stable compatibility facades.
falsifiers: If a proposed slice has only one unstable call site and no reusable decision contract, keep it local rather than creating another engine.
If extraction requires changing receipt bytes, database ordering, error taxonomy, or replay identity without a migration, reject the extraction.
If an adapter can bypass the injected planner without an OOPTDD failure, the boundary is not load-bearing.
